narration: The pipeline begins with a pre-trained 3D Gaussian Splatting scene model, whose initial parameters remain frozen.
Next, Frequency Guided Densification, or FGD, is introduced to adapt the Gaussian primitives based on spatial frequency.
In Phase 1 of FGD, the contribution of each 3D Gaussian to rendering quality is assessed, pruning low-impact Gaussians to reduce redundancy.
In Phase 2, multi-view renders are patchified and analyzed via Discrete Fourier Transform with a quadratic mask, splitting Gaussians located in high-frequency regions.
The densified representation G prime o is obtained, and parameter-specific gradient masks are constructed to guide subsequent learning.
Parameters are unfrozen to form the fine-tuned model G w, which is rendered differentiably into 2D viewpoints.
A Discrete Wavelet Transform separates the rendered view, passing low-frequency components into a pre-trained decoder to recover the embedded message under message loss L m.
Finally, high-frequency wavelet loss and image reconstruction losses combine into the total loss, directing the masked optimizer to update the watermarked 3D Gaussians.
